hints: Look carefully at what a skeletal structure is really telling you, with every unlabeled corner and end representing a carbon atom.
Count the labelled nitrogens first, then count the carbon corners, you should find 4 nitrogens and 6 carbons.
Work out how many hydrogens each carbon needs to make four bonds, then simplify that full molecular formula to its smallest whole number ratio.
walkthrough:
**Read the skeletal structure**

Remember, in skeletal structures every vertex that is not labelled is a carbon atom. Here the four $\text{N}$ atoms are labelled, so all the other corners are $\text{C}$.

Counting gives:
$$\text{N atoms} = 4, \quad \text{C atoms} = 6$$

**Add the hidden hydrogens**

Each carbon must have four bonds in total. In this cage, each carbon is joined to two nitrogens by single bonds, so it needs two more bonds.

That means each carbon is a $\text{CH}_2$ group:
$$6 \times \text{CH}_2 = \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$$
So the molecular formula is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4$.

**Convert to the empirical formula**

Empirical means the simplest whole number ratio. All the subscripts 6, 12 and 4 can be divided by 2:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4 \rightarrow \text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{N}_2$$
This is the simplest ratio and matches one of the options.

options.A: Not correct. $\text{CH}_2\text{N}$ would multiply up to $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{N}_4$ or $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_6$, neither of which matches the true count of 6 carbons and 4 nitrogens. It comes from dividing by the wrong factor and losing the correct C to N ratio.
options.B: Correct. The structure contains 6 $\text{CH}_2$ groups and 4 N atoms, giving molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4$. Dividing by 2 gives the simplest whole number ratio $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{N}_2$.
options.C: Not correct. $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{N}_4$ keeps 4 nitrogens but only counts 4 carbons. This is the common trap of miscounting the carbon corners in the 3D cage drawing and missing two $\text{CH}_2$ groups.
options.D: Not correct. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{N}_4$ is the molecular formula of hexamine, correctly counted, but the question asks for the empirical formula. You must simplify this by dividing by 2 to get the simplest ratio.
